explainer.title: How committee rank works
paragraphs: Each senator usually sits on two major committees and may also take one smaller standing committee: Budget, Rules, Small Business, Veterans' Affairs or Aging. Select committees such as Ethics and Indian Affairs have no limit.

Three major committees rank above the rest: Appropriations, Armed Services and Finance. Both parties let a senator sit on only one of them, so a senator on Finance takes their second major seat on a committee such as Judiciary or Commerce. Republicans add Foreign Relations to that list; Democrats, who run the incoming Senate, do not.
Appropriations writes the spending bills, Finance handles taxes, Medicare and Social Security, and Armed Services writes the defense bill.

SSAP.label: Top committee
SSAP.note: One of the three committees that both parties' rules treat as most senior: a senator is generally limited to one of them.

SSAS.note: One of the three committees that both parties' rules treat as most senior: a senator is generally limited to one of them.

SSFI.label: Top committee
SSFI.note: One of the three committees that both parties' rules treat as most senior: a senator is generally limited to one of them.

SSFR.label: Major committee
SSFR.note: A major committee. Republican party rules also count it among the most senior; Democratic rules do not.

SSAF.label: Major committee
SSAF.note: A major committee: a senator serves on two of these.

SSJU.note: A major committee: a senator serves on two of these.

SSBU.label: Standing committee
SSBU.note: A standing committee, but not a major one: a senator may serve on only one of these, counting Aging.

SSRA.label: Standing committee
SSRA.note: A standing committee, but not a major one: a senator may serve on only one of these, counting Aging.

SSSB.label: Standing committee
SSSB.note: A standing committee, but not a major one: a senator may serve on only one of these, counting Aging.

SSVA.label: Standing committee
SSVA.note: A standing committee, but not a major one: a senator may serve on only one of these, counting Aging.

SLIN.label: Select committee
SLIN.note: A select committee, created for a specific purpose and now permanent. It counts as a major committee when senators are assigned (Senate Resolution 445, 2004).

SLET.label: Select committee
SLET.note: A select committee, created for a specific purpose and now permanent. A senator may serve on it in addition to other committees.

SPAG.label: Special committee
SPAG.note: A special committee, created for a specific purpose and now permanent. It counts toward a senator's one lighter-limit assignment, with the standing committees such as Budget.

SLIA.label: Select or special committee
SLIA.note: Not one of the 16 standing committees; the Senate counts it among its four special or select committees. A senator may serve on it in addition to other committees.

SCNC.label: Caucus
SCNC.note: Not a committee: the Senate's one officially recognized caucus, set up by law in 1985.
